tools.name: lookup_company_free
tools.description: How many open jobs does this company have today, and is it hiring more or less than last week? Free sample, no API key, 10 calls a day per caller: says whether the company is tracked, today's open-role count and, once the series is long enough, the 7-day change. Compiled by an AI from public careers

tools.name: get_company_open_roles
tools.description: Daily history of open jobs for one company: open-role count per day and per department, and the careers board it comes from. Needs a free API key (300 calls a day). Compiled by an AI from public careers boards, not human-reviewed; removal on request.

tools.name: get_hiring_changes
tools.description: Which companies changed their number of open jobs on a given day (hiring more or cutting roles), largest change first. Needs a free API key (300 calls a day). Compiled by an AI from public careers boards, not human-reviewed; removal on request.

tools.name: coverage
tools.description: How many companies and careers boards are tracked and how many days have been captured. No key needed.

tools.name: request_api_key
tools.description: Email a free API key link (300 calls a day) to the user's address. Ask the user for their email first; they open the link once to see the key, then set it as the x-api-key header of this connection.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_api_key · Private data: lookup_company_free, get_company_open_roles, get_hiring_changes, request_api_key · Public sink: request_api_key.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_api_key · Private data: lookup_company_free, get_company_open_roles, get_hiring_changes, request_api_key · Public sink: request_api_key

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
